question: During 2015, in, ______ sector, Government of India had allowed about 49% of FDI.
solution:
The correct answer is __**defence**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During 2015, the Government of India allowed about **49% of FDI** in the **defence sector**.
 
• This decision was part of a broader effort to boost the defense manufacturing capabilities in India, encouraging foreign companies to invest and form joint ventures with Indian firms.
 
• The aim was to modernize the defense sector and reduce dependency on imports by encouraging indigenous production.
 
• This policy change was expected to bring in advanced technology, foster innovation, and create employment opportunities in the defense manufacturing sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy** in India is regulated by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.
 
• The policy framework for FDI is governed by the **Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA)**.
 
• The FDI policy aims to attract foreign investment, enhance technology transfer, and improve the overall competitiveness of the Indian economy.
 
• FDI in certain sectors is subject to sectoral caps and approval requirements, while in other sectors, it is allowed under the automatic route.
 
• Over the years, the Government of India has liberalized the FDI policy to make India an attractive destination for foreign investors.
